summary.text: A 16-year-old woman consulted in the emergency room for asthenia of 2 months duration that worsened over the last 15 days, with increased menstrual bleeding and hair loss, and a history of atopic dermatitis and a familial history of acute myeloid leukemia. She had paleness, petechiae in the lower limbs and a 3 cm scalp patch of alopecia.

Blood tests showed a marked microcytic anemia, a high reticulocyte count, a severely low platelet count, a low ferritin of 8.60 ng/ml and a moderate increase in liver enzymes. She was admitted to the Hematology ward, and a bone marrow study showed hypercellularity with megakaryocytic and erythroid hyperplasia. A diagnosis of ITP and iron deficiency anemia was made.

Intravenous immunoglobulins gave no significant platelet increase after 48 h. Prednisone 2 mg per kg was started for platelet counts under 10 × 10^(9 )/L for 5 days, with platelets rising to 70 × 10^(9 )/L on day 5; iron supplements were started and she was discharged. At the 12-day follow-up platelets had dropped, corticosteroids were reinstated for another 5 days, and hemoglobin returned to normal after 2 weeks of iron.

At discharge she was referred to Dermatology and diagnosed with alopecia areata, treated for a year with prednisone 0.5 mg per kg with partial response while platelet counts were normal. When corticosteroids were stopped alopecia worsened and platelets dropped below 100 × 10^(9 )/L. Baricitinib 4 mg/day was then started off-label, with a platelet count of 70 × 10^(9 )/L 2 years after the initial episode, leading to the diagnosis of chronic ITP.

Alopecia improved after 3 months of baricitinib with good tolerance, platelet counts rose above 150 × 10^(9 )/L and the anti-microsomal antibodies fell to 167.5 IU/ml. The dose was reduced to 2 mg/day after 18 months and stopped 6 months later with maintained hair regrowth, and platelet counts remained within normal levels at 4 years follow-up.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not decide which platelet count at diagnosis is correct.
ambiguities.issue: The text prints a platelet count of 6 × 10^(9 )/L from the blood tests (Table 1) while the Table 1 platelet row prints 7 × 10^(9)/L. Both are kept as review-only source-conflict facts.

evidence.quote: severe thrombocytopenia of 6 × 10^(9 )/L

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not correct the printed hemoglobin value.
ambiguities.issue: Table 1 prints hemoglobin as 660 g/L against a printed range of 110–156 g/L, while the text reports a marked microcytic anemia; the printed value is implausible but kept as printed and not corrected.

evidence.quote: Hemoglobin | 660 g/L (110–156 g/L)
a marked microcytic anemia

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not decide when the anti-microsomal antibodies in Table 1 were measured.
ambiguities.issue: Table 1 is titled Complementary tests at diagnosis and prints anti-microsomal antibodies of 8547 U/ml, while the text says the anti-microsomal (anti-TPO) antibodies (8,547 UI/ml) were measured later, when corticosteroids were discontinued. The unit is spelled U/ml, UI/ml and IU/ml in different places. The discussion also places the high anti-TPO titers just before baricitinib treatment.

evidence.quote: Anti-microsomal antibodies | 8547 U/ml (5–60 U/ml)
At that time anti-microsomal autoantibodies, also known as anti-TPO antibodies, (8,547 UI/ml) were measured
Our patient had high titers of anti-TPO antibodies together with a slight decrease in platelet counts and a worsening of her alopecia areata, just before baricitinib treatment.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assign a time to the autoimmune screening or the NGS panel beyond what each sentence states.
ambiguities.issue: Table 1 lists the autoimmune screening rows and the NGS panel under tests at diagnosis, while the text describes the screening (citing Table 1) and the NGS panel after the anti-microsomal measurement when corticosteroids were discontinued. The table-only rows keep the caption time; the screening text fact and the NGS fact (table row and text describe the same single 192-gene panel with the same result) carry no time, and their event is ordered only before baricitinib by the word then.

evidence.quote: A screening for other autoimmune diseases was performed, with no significant findings (Table 1).
Moreover, a next generation sequencing (NGS) panel of 192 genes related to immune dysregulation found no pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not decide the cause of the platelet recovery or of the remission.
ambiguities.issue: The authors state that the link between baricitinib and the platelet improvement remains speculative and that spontaneous ITP remission may have occurred; no causal fact is recorded.

evidence.quote: so the association between baricitinib treatment and platelet improvement remains speculative

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer a platelet unit for the 12-day follow-up count.
ambiguities.issue: The 12-day follow-up platelet count is printed as 6 × 10^(9) without /L; no unit is added.

evidence.quote: platelet counts dropped to 6 × 10^(9)

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record thyroid disease or a secondary ITP as a diagnosis.
ambiguities.issue: The discussion says the anti-TPO findings could be coincidental and that thyroid disease as a cause of a secondary ITP cannot be confirmed; no thyroid or secondary-ITP condition is recorded.

evidence.quote: These findings could be coincidental and the association of thyroid disease as a cause of a secondary ITP cannot be confirmed.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not equate the figure's AA complete response label or its IVIG dose with text facts.
ambiguities.issue: Figure 1 prints an IVIG dose of 1g/kg body weight and an AA complete response marker that the text does not state; these are pixel content in visual.json only.

article_limitations: One index patient. Table 1 (Complementary tests at diagnosis) holds one time point only, so it is not a serial measurement table.

Source conflict: the text prints a platelet count of 6 × 10^(9 )/L from the blood tests it cites as Table 1, and Table 1 prints 7 × 10^(9)/L; two plausible numbers for one measurement, both review-only.
Table 1 prints hemoglobin as 660 g/L with a 110–156 g/L reference range although the text reports marked anemia; recorded as printed, review-only.

Table 1 puts the anti-microsomal antibodies, the autoimmune screening and the NGS panel under tests at diagnosis while the text places them later, when corticosteroids were discontinued; the anti-microsomal facts are review-only and the NGS and screening text facts carry no time.
Figure 1 is a chart of platelet count, anti-TPO antibodies, treatments and disease course whose plotted values are pixel content only; no values are read from the plot.
No supplementary material is listed in the source or the raw XML.
